answer.label: Spurgeon attribution unverified
answer.sourceLine: The Spurgeon Library rejects this exact line and points to a different wave-and-Rock image in Sin and Grace. Dallas Theological Seminary’s book excerpt likewise warns that the exact wording is debated. Desiring God shows the attribution circulating in 2013, but provides no original Spurgeon location. No creator for this compact sentence has been established.

context.heading: The setting behind the words
lead: The documented Spurgeon image concerns a wave of temptation strengthening someone’s grip on the Rock of Ages. The popular kiss-the-wave line turns that image into a compact first-person declaration. A related image is a useful comparison, but cannot establish that exact declaration as his. Spurgeon Library correction ↗
